status.summary: TierPoint's Omaha - Midlands page, in its version modified on 3 September 2026, describes 'this energy-efficient and resilient TierPoint Omaha (Midlands) data center and colocation facility' with LEED Gold and Energy Star certifications, says 'This secure data center in Papillion, NE, is part of our nationwide network of data centers' and gives 'Omaha - Midlands (MID) 11425 South 84th Street Papillion, NE 68046' with 63,000+ total square feet, 15,000+ square feet of raised floor, cabinets and cages available, two 2.25 MW redundant generators and a carrier-neutral facility. This records the facility as operating on 3 September 2026, the modification day of the captured version (bounded below by the Internet Archive copy of 2 July 2026, which carries dateModified 2024-07-31, and confirmed by the Internet Archive copy of 9 October 2026); it is not an opening date, and generator ratings are not IT load.

locator.precision: Centroid of the union of the four Sarpy County condominium-unit parcels of the Midlands Data Center Condominium at 11425 S 84th St, Papillion (parcels 011591834, 011591835, 011591836 and 011591837; units 1-4, 25% each). The county draws the units as two stacked schematic rectangles, about 21 by 47 m in all (935 m2), inside an otherwise unparcelled lot of about 4.1 acres enclosed by Huntington Park Replat 5 and neighbouring parcels. It locates the data-centre condominium building property, not TierPoint's suite.
locator.identity_review: TierPoint gives 'Omaha - Midlands (MID) 11425 South 84th Street Papillion, NE 68046'. A Sarpy County query for site addresses beginning '11425 S 84' returns exactly the four units of the MIDLANDS DATA CENTER CONDOMINIUM: units 3 and 4 owned by TierPoint Properties LLC and units 1 and 2 by Alegent Health, a health-system organisation. TierPoint's own structured-data point (41.13467, -96.039021) lies 27.2 m east of the selected centroid, inside the same unparcelled condominium lot, and is used only as a cross-check. The county's geodata.sarpy.gov host blocks automated clients, so the county's CC0 hosted layer listed on its GIS hub is used, as for the published TierPoint Omaha - Bellevue record. No geocoder or city centre is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: Sarpy County publishes no positional accuracy for parcel polygons, the layer is a December 2023 snapshot and the condominium units are drawn schematically; the building footprint and the position of TierPoint's space within the 4.1-acre lot are not published.

additions.site_name: Google Project Skyway data center campus (Pine Island Industrial PUD, Pine Island, Minnesota)
additions.name: Google Project Skyway — proposed data-center campus on the Pine Island Industrial PUD site with four Google-owned substations (PUC route-permit docket E002/TL-26-135)

status.summary: The Minnesota Public Utilities Commission's notice of public hearings and availability of a draft permit, issued 31 August 2026 in docket E002/TL-26-135, identifies the application of Xcel Energy and Echo Zone LLC, a subsidiary of Google LLC, for a 1.2-mile 345 kV line from Xcel's North Rochester Substation to four new substation facilities at the proposed Pine Island Industrial Planned Unit Development site, and states that the four Project Skyway substations will be owned and operated by Google; it also records Xcel's petition for an electric service agreement with Echo Zone (docket E002/M-26-170). Google announced on 24 February 2026 that Pine Island will be the future home of a Google data center supplied by Xcel Energy. The project is therefore recorded as an announced Google data-center campus on 31 August 2026. The route permit is only a draft (14 August 2026), the line serves rather than consents to the data center, no city site plan or building permit was reviewed, and the May 2027 construction start and December 2029 in-service date are forecasts.

locator.precision: Centroid of the single 'Project Skyway Approximate Location' polygon (layer 13 of the State of Minnesota Skyway_WFL1 service behind the PUC project map for docket 26-135): about 497 geodesic acres, a strip about 0.77 by 3.07 km east of US 52 in the City of Pine Island and Pine Island Township, Goodhue County. It locates the approximate campus land, not any building; the four proposed Google substations lie in its southern half, about 0.7 km south of the point.
locator.identity_review: The PUC notice names the Project Skyway substations at the proposed Pine Island Industrial PUD site and Google as their owner and operator; all four 'Proposed Substations' polygons of the same state service lie inside the selected polygon, as do the EQB record points of the Project Skyway AUAR and of the transmission-line notice. The polygon matches the Project Skyway AUAR area adopted by the City of Pine Island (Resolution 25-42, 16 September 2025): about 482 acres bounded by 490th Street, Trunk Highway 52 and 195th Avenue. Google's 24 February 2026 post identifies its Pine Island project as a data center served by Xcel Energy. The City of Pine Island website disallows all agents and Goodhue County is not in the MnGeo open parcel compilation (which returns no Echo Zone parcel), so no parcel union is used. No geocoder, city centre or zone centroid is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The state labels the polygon an approximate location and publishes no positional accuracy; the centroid represents an approximately 500-acre campus whose building layout and parcels were not reviewed.

The operator's pages give 1623 Farnam Street, Omaha, and describe its Omaha Interconnected Edge Data Center of 75,000 square feet with 6 MW of power. These present-tense statements record the carrier hotel as operating on 20 August 2026, the post's publication day; it is not an opening date, and the power figure is an operator specification, not measured load.

ATC's 15 September 2026 release ties the revised Ozaukee County Distribution Interconnection application to 'increased electric load in the Port Washington area' and to 'The customer at the Lighthouse campus', its project page names 'the Port Washington data center project' as the need and gives PSCW docket 137-CE-229, and Oracle's 16 September 2026 blog says Oracle is partnering with ATC on that revised application to serve the Project Lighthouse campus. context_updates.summary: On 15 September 2026 ATC announced that it had filed a revised application with the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin (docket 137-CE-229) for the Ozaukee County Distribution Interconnection Project, which it says is needed for increased electric load in the Port Washington area and whose transmission cost the customer at the Lighthouse campus has committed to fund in full through its rates. The project would add up to five substations, including the proposed Decker Substation in Port Washington joined to the grid by two new dual-circuit 345-kV lines, plus new and rebuilt 345-kV lines across six counties; ATC filed first in September 2025, and the PSCW revoked that application's completeness determination before the revised filing. Oracle's 16 September 2026 blog says it is partnering with ATC on the revised application and that more than half of the campus's power capacity will come from carbon-free sources. Power-readiness context only: the transmission works are proposed and not approved (ATC's milestones put construction 31 days after a PSCW order and in-service about 17 months later, both forecasts), and the campus's status, observation date, location and capacity are unchanged.

context_updates.summary: Alliant Energy, the utility serving Beaver Dam, states on its data-centers page (captured 27 October 2026; Alliant's sitemap gives it lastmod 26 October 2026) and in its 12 November 2025 release that Meta will underwrite nearly USD 200 million in energy network improvements - network upgrades, utility substations and transmission lines - to support the Beaver Dam data center, which it says will be built in Alliant Energy's Beaver Dam Commerce Park, and that the site's electricity use will be matched with 100% clean and renewable energy; Meta will also give USD 15 million to Alliant's Hometown Care Energy Fund over ten years.
